text:
maya: Customer hitting 403 on /v1/generate after rotating keys yesterday. They say calls worked before rotation. Request ID they see: req_0a1b2c3d

sam: thanks — can you paste the original curl they used and the x-redwood-* headers?

maya: sure, pasted from customer chat (redacted token):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXREDACTED" \
  -H "x-redwood-org-id: org_abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-std-1","input":"hello"}'
```

eli: quick check: different teams sometimes rotate project keys vs org keys. If they used a project-scoped key but set org header for a different org we get HMAC/aud mismatch -> 403. Any customer logs?

maya: customer provided portion of server logs: 
```
WARN auth: token scope mismatch: expected aud=org:invoke org=org_abc123 got aud=project:run proj=proj-x9
ERROR request req_0a1b2c3d: auth failed status=403 reason=aud_mismatch
```

jordan: @maya can you ask for the full debug bundle (curl -v + X-Request-Id response headers + timestamp) so we can map to internal ingest? Also ask them to run the curl with -H "x-redwood-project-id" removed/added to test.

maya: asked for bundle and a fresh curl with --dump-header. Customer sent response headers showing: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 18:12:34 GMT
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
content-type: application/json
```

support-bot: Log link created: https://logs.redwood.internal/ingest/req_0a1b2c3d (internal) :information_source:

sam: thanks. I pulled the internal entry (sanitized):
```
auth_checker.go: verifySignature failed: token_claims.aud="project:run" required="org:invoke"
attached_key=svc_proj_key:proj-x9 owner=project:proj-x9
```

eli: confirms: customer accidentally used a project service key for org-scoped endpoint. Two remediation options: 1) issue a new org-scoped key to the customer, or 2) call the project-scoped endpoints (they exist but different base path). Which they prefer?

maya: customer asked for minimal repro steps to validate on their side before key swap. I suggested this curl to reproduce the 403 when using proj key against org endpoint:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_proj_ABCDEF" \
  -H "x-redwood-org-id: org_abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-std-1","input":"test"}'
```

sam: and this to validate success using org-scoped key (or remove org header if calling project endpoint):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_org_NEWKEY" \
  -H "x-redwood-org-id: org_abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-std-1","input":"test"}'
```

eli: also ask them to include the returned x-request-id header in the debug bundle and timestamp when they ran it so we can correlate to token issuance events.

maya: customer returned with quick test: proj key + org header produced 403 exactly as above. They tested org key and it worked. They want a short writeup to send their security team why this happened.

sam: wrote this blurb for them: "Root cause: key audience (aud) mismatch. The rotated key was scoped to a project (aud=project:run) but requests were sent to an org-level endpoint that requires org-scoped keys (aud=org:invoke). The platform rejects tokens whose 'aud' claim doesn't match endpoint expectations, returning 403 with request id in x-request-id. Remediation: use the org-scoped key for org endpoints or use the project-specific endpoints for project keys. Rotate keys only after ensuring downstream clients are updated."

jordan: I've added a short internal note to KB: `auth: how aud/scope maps to endpoints` and linked example cURLs + debug-bundle checklist.

maya: customer happy, will rotate to org key and confirm. closing? :thumbsup:

eli: mark resolved once customer confirms, leave incident tag if we need to update onboarding docs.

maya: will follow up tomorrow and drop final confirmation in thread. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
